channel.title: interviews on Loud Legends
channel.description: Recent content in interviews on Loud Legends

item.title: The Problem With 'LOAD' and 'RELOAD', According to JAMES HETFIELD: 'I Hate That Part Of Us'
item.description: Metallica made a name for itself in the early days with fast, aggressive thrash metal. But things changed with the release of their self-titled album in 1991, known to most as the Black Album.

item.title: What Growing Up Was Like for DAVE MUSTAINE: 'My Dad Drank A Lot And Was Abusive'
item.description: Dave Mustaine, the founder of Megadeth and one of heavy metal’s most recognizable voices, has lived a life filled with music, fame, and success. But behind the guitars and sold-out shows is a past that’s far less glamorous.

item.title: Michael Paget Says BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE's New Album Will Feature 'Crazy Tuning'
item.description: Guitarist Michael “Padge” Paget says BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE is exploring new territory on their next studio album, including tunings the band has never used before. The longtime member of the Welsh metalcore group opened up about the upcoming record during a chat at this year’s Download Festival in the UK (watch the interview below).

item.title: KITTIE’s MORGAN LANDER Talks About Writing 'FIRE': 'It Was A Relearning Curve'
item.description: Getting back in the studio after more than a decade isn’t as simple as picking up where you left off. Just ask Morgan Lander. The guitarist and vocalist for Canadian metal band KITTIE says that writing Fire, their first album in 13 years, didn’t come with muscle memory (via TotalRock).

item.title: Creed's SCOTT STAPP On Viral Revival: 'It Started Online Before We Even Noticed'
item.description: Scott Stapp says the Creed reunion didn’t start with a grand plan or a flashy PR campaign. It began with the internet doing its thing. In a recent interview (via Meltdown), the singer explained that the band started to see signs of renewed interest around 2020, when clips, memes, and jokes about Creed started to go viral.

item.title: Dave 'PHOENIX' Farrell Talks LINKIN PARK’s Return: 'Time Doesn’t Heal The Wound, It Changes The Lens'
item.description: Linkin Park is back on tour with a new album and new members. But for bassist Dave “Phoenix” Farrell, returning to the band after Chester Bennington’s death was not easy.

item.title: Evanescence's AMY LEE Reflects On Pandemic-Era Lessons: 'Who Knows When This Will Ever End? So Let’s Put Out Our Music'
item.description: Amy Lee says the pandemic changed how Evanescence approaches releasing music. In a recent interview with WDHA-FM, the singer explained that waiting for a perfect moment to drop a full album no longer feels realistic.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD Reveals How the 'Terrible' LARS ULRICH Convinced Him to Start METALLICA
item.description: James Hetfield remembers the first time he met Lars Ulrich. According to him, Lars wasn’t exactly a great drummer when they crossed paths. Still, something about his energy made a lasting impression.

item.title: The Backstage Incident That Made KERRY KING Call a Rock Icon a 'Complete Jerk'
item.description: Not everyone in the world of music gets along, and that includes some of its biggest stars. Even in heavy metal, a genre known for its intensity and larger-than-life personalities, there are musicians who just don’t click.

item.title: AMY LEE Says New EVANESCENCE Album Coming 'Probably Early Next Year'
item.description: Evanescence is working on their next studio album, and according to Amy Lee, it’s likely to arrive in early 2026. The singer gave an update during a recent interview with WDHA-FM 105.

item.title: Dave 'PHOENIX' Farrell Breaks Silence on CHESTER BENNINGTON’s Death: 'Is It Even Called LINKIN PARK Anymore?'
item.description: Linkin Park bassist Dave “Phoenix” Farrell opened up about the band’s long road back to music after the loss of lead singer Chester Bennington. In a new interview with Czech station Evropa 2 (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: The Genre DAVE GROHL Called 'Too Easy' And Blamed for Making ROCK DUMBER
item.description: Dave Grohl has always been a believer in loud guitars, big feelings, and not overthinking things. Foo Fighters, the band he’s fronted since the mid-’90s, built a career on that formula: simple riffs, catchy choruses, and performances that sometimes go off the rails, in a good way.

item.title: SCOTT STAPP Says CREED Is Rebuilding: 'We're Talking About New Music'
item.description: CREED frontman Scott Stapp says the band is easing back into things after more than a decade apart. In a recent interview, he shared that the group has been spending time together, reflecting on the past, and having early conversations about making new music (via Meltdown) (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: Morgan Lander Says KITTIE May Release More Music: 'We’re Enjoying Ourselves'
item.description: KITTIE could be back in the studio again soon. Guitarist and vocalist Morgan Lander says the band is open to releasing more new music, thanks to the positive energy surrounding their recent reunion (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: The Night SLASH Felt Deep Shame Over GUNS N’ ROSES’ Treatment of METALLICA: 'I Lost Their Respect'
item.description: Back in the early ’90s, Guns N’ Roses were living the full-throttle rockstar fantasy, loud, chaotic, and unapologetic. Their shows were wild, their image untamed, and their reputation built on pushing limits.

item.title: The Emotional METALLICA Song That Wasn’t Meant to Be, According to JAMES HETFIELD
item.description: When Load dropped in June 1996, it marked a sharp left turn for Metallica. The band traded speed and aggression for a slower, more reflective sound. That shift didn’t land well with everyone, but it did show fans a broader side of the band’s musical identity.

item.title: BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE's Michael Paget On New Album: 'It's Gonna Be Super Heavy'
item.description: BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE is working on new music, and according to guitarist Michael “Padge” Paget, fans should expect something heavier than ever before. The Welsh metal band recently cut its joint tour with Trivium short, choosing to focus instead on writing and recording their next studio album.

item.title: The Unusual Way AC/DC's ANGUS YOUNG Came Up With the Chorus of 'HIGHWAY TO HELL'
item.description: Angus Young, lead guitarist and founding member of AC/DC, shared a rather unexpected story about how he wrote one of rock’s most iconic choruses. Speaking in a 2021 interview with Essentials Radio on Apple Music (via Kerrang), Young explained how the chorus of “Highway to Hell” came to him, not in a studio or during rehearsal, but while he was on a bathroom break.

item.title: The One Thing That Could End MEGADETH, According to DAVE MUSTAINE
item.description: Megadeth has been going strong for four decades, led from day one by guitarist, vocalist, and founding member Dave Mustaine. He’s the only constant in the thrash metal band’s long history and the driving force behind many of its best-known songs, including “Peace Sells,” “In My Darkest Hour,” “Holy Wars… The Punishment Due,” “Symphony of Destruction,” “A Tout Le Monde,” and “Trust.

item.title: MEGADETH's DAVE MUSTAINE On the 'Puppy Incident': 'JAMES Got Punched In The Mouth. He Kicked My Dog'
item.description: There’s no elegant way to introduce a story that ends with James Hetfield catching a mouthful of knuckles. Especially when the instigating factor was a puppy. But here we are.

item.title: Sodom's TOM ANGELRIPPER On Modern Metal Production: 'It's Cheap And It Shows'
item.description: Tom Angelripper has no patience for how modern metal is made. From his perspective, today’s studio habits cut corners and it’s obvious. “Recording in a digital way is cheap,” he said (via Blabbermouth).

item.title: Ex-EXODUS RICK HUNOLT Looks Back On Thrash Origins: 'We Inspired METALLICA And SLAYER'
item.description: Ex-EXODUS guitarist Rick Hunolt didn’t bother dancing around it during a recent chat with Pod Scum host Rexx Ruger (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.NET). When Ruger put Hunolt and Gary Holt on the same tier as Hetfield/Hammett or Hanneman/King, Hunolt didn’t blink.

item.title: CHARLIE BENANTE Says BLACK SABBATH Helped Shape ANTHRAX’s Sound: 'We Covered Sabbath Bloody Sabbath'
item.description: Anthrax drummer Charlie Benante pointed to Black Sabbath as a key influence on the band’s formative sound, recalling how their admiration for the Birmingham pioneers led them to cover Sabbath Bloody Sabbath during a formative period in their career.

item.title: The One AC/DC Song ANGUS YOUNG Struggles to Play Live
item.description: Few bands are as famously built on no-nonsense riffs as AC/DC. For Angus Young and his brother Malcolm, there was no mystery to their formula: loud guitars, open chords, and choruses made for the crowd to scream in unison.

item.title: EUGENE ABDUKHANOV On MESHUGGAH's Early Days: 'People Didn’t Get It Then'
item.description: Eugene Abdukhanov isn’t new to giving credit where it’s due, even if it takes the rest of the world a couple of decades to catch up. Sitting down with Forever Loud at Download Festival, the JINJER bassist pulled no punches while looking back on what it was like watching MESHUGGAH rise from being the metal kid no one invited to the party, to becoming the very sound system (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: Why Limp Bizkit’s FRED DURST Always Wore That RED BASEBALL CAP
item.description: Back in the early 2000s, nu metal was dominating the rock scene, with bands like Slipknot, Korn, Kid Rock, and Linkin Park in constant rotation on MTV.

item.title: The Heavy METALLICA Song That Tells the Story of JAMES HETFIELD’s Childhood TRAUMA
item.description: James Hetfield, guitarist and frontman of Metallica, didn’t exactly grow up riding rainbows. His early years were marked by the rigid dogma of a household that followed Christian Science, a belief system founded by Lafayette Ronald Hubbard (yep, the same guy behind Scientology).

item.title: STEVE DIGIORGIO On Recording With DAVE MUSTAINE: 'He Wasn't What I Expected'
item.description: Steve DiGiorgio, longtime bassist for Testament, has spoken candidly about his brief but intense experience recording with Dave Mustaine for Megadeth’s album The Sick, The Dying… And The Dead!

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD’s Favorite Thrash Bands (That Aren’t METALLICA, SLAYER, MEGADETH or ANTHRAX)
item.description: At this point, saying Metallica “isn’t thrash anymore” is like complaining MTV doesn’t play music videos. Welcome to the last three decades. Sure, the band traded speed for stadiums a while back, but try telling the IRS they’re not the face of thrash metal and see how that goes.

item.title: AMY LEE Talks About EMMA ANZAI Joining EVANESCENCE: 'I Called Her First'
item.description: Evanescence frontwoman Amy Lee has opened up about the band’s evolving lineup and her longtime connection with bassist Emma Anzai, offering rare insight into the decision-making behind the group’s most recent personnel shift.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On the 'Weak' METALLICA Member: 'Not Amazing'
item.description: James Hetfield has always been particular when it comes to Metallica’s music. Known for his precision as a rhythm guitarist, he’s often regarded as the most technically sharp member of the band, along with current bassist Robert Trujillo.

item.title: Ex-Pantera TERRY GLAZE On DIMEBAG's Death: 'It Didn't Hit Me Until I Saw The Dirt'
item.description: Former Pantera vocalist Terry Glaze has shared a personal account of how he learned about the death of guitarist “Dimebag” Darrell Abbott and the emotional aftermath that followed.

item.title: PAUL STANLEY On KISS Reunion Regrets: 'Some Nights Were Awful'
item.description: Turns out the face paint couldn’t cover everything. Back in 2000, KISS slapped the word farewell on a tour, grabbed the original lineup, and hit the road like it was 1977 all over again.

item.title: AVENGED SEVENFOLD's M. SHADOWS On Being Misunderstood: 'People Are Just Getting It Now'
item.description: M. Shadows isn’t mad. He’s just… already moved on. If Life Is But a Dream… finally makes sense to you in 2025, congrats on solving the puzzle.

item.title: KORN Praises SLEEP TOKEN's Download Festival Show: 'They Outdid a SLIPKNOT Stage'
item.description: The members of Korn had high praise for Sleep Token following their performance at the Download Festival on Saturday, June 14. According to the band, the masked group managed to silence skeptics with a massive stage setup and commanding live presence.

item.title: The Day KORN Knocked a Guy Out Mid-Show… and Then WROTE A SONG About It
item.description: Not every song is born in a studio with clean instruments and sober minds. Some, like Korn’s Clown, crawl out of drug-fueled all-nighters in dingy apartments, shaped as much by the chaos around them as by the riffs themselves.

item.title: SHARON OSBOURNE Talks About IRON MAIDEN Drama: 'It’s Just The Singer I Can’t Stand'
item.description: Sharon Osbourne still hasn’t let it go. Two decades after the absolute circus that was Ozzfest 2005, she’s perfectly willing to laugh about sabotaging Iron Maiden with beans, pre-recorded sound effects, and strategic sound cuts.

item.title: RINGO STARR Slams ROGER DALTREY Over Firing Of Son: 'Never Liked How That Little Man Runs The Band'
item.description: Zak Starkey didn’t bother hiding his disappointment after being pushed out of The Who, a gig he held for nearly 30 years as the band’s live drummer. It all unraveled after a messy show at the Royal Albert Hall earlier this year, which ultimately triggered the official announcement of his departure in April.

item.title: LARS ULRICH Says Younger Fans Ignore METALLICA Classics: 'They're More Into the New Stuff'
item.description: Not every Metallica fan has Master of Puppets tattooed on their brain. According to Lars Ulrich, a surprising number of listeners are skipping the band’s old-school thrash masterpieces in favor of more recent material.

item.title: JESSE LEACH Talks About KILLSWITCH ENGAGE's 'Aftermath': 'We All Have a Responsibility'
item.description: Killswitch Engage isn’t wasting time with metaphors or feel-good slogans in their latest single. The video for “Aftermath” just dropped, and it doesn’t sugarcoat a thing. If you were expecting a fun, breakdown-heavy anthem about “staying strong,” keep scrolling.

item.title: DAVID ELLEFSON Says MEGADETH Took Credit For 'Soldier On!': 'Just Wiped My Name Off'
item.description: David Ellefson isn’t done unpacking his past with Megadeth,and he’s brought receipts. In a new interview with The Delz Show, the former bassist draws some not-so-subtle contrasts between how Metallica handled songwriting credits with Dave Mustaine and how Mustaine allegedly did the opposite when it came to Megadeth’s own track, Soldier On!

item.title: BRIAN WELCH on KORN's New Album: 'We're Doing It All On Tape'
item.description: Korn is back in the studio, but don’t expect any instant gratification. This time, they’re ditching modern convenience for a much older, sweatier process. During a chat with BBC Radio 1’s Rock Show With Daniel P Carter (as transcribed by The PRP, guitarist Brian “Head” Welch explained that the band has fully embraced analog recording.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On His Father's Abandonment: 'He Didn't Even Say Goodbye'
item.description: Before the arenas, awards, and global tours, James Hetfield was just a kid growing up in the suburbs of Los Angeles. The setting looked ideal from the outside.

item.title: BLACK SABBATH's Tony Iommi Talks About Final Show Concerns: 'The Unknown Worries Me'
item.description: Tony Iommi, the ever-present architect of Black Sabbath, isn’t exactly sleeping easy as the band’s farewell inches closer. Set for July 5 in Birmingham, England, the hometown gig isn’t just another concert.

item.title: PIGGY D. On Working With MARILYN MANSON: 'I'm Proud To Stand Next To Him'
item.description: Matt Montgomery, better known as Piggy D., isn’t shy when it comes to describing his experience playing bass for Marilyn Manson. In a recent interview with Radioactive MikeZ on 96.

item.title: IHSAHN Explains Why GHOST, SLEEP TOKEN And SLIPKNOT Attract Crowds: 'It's The Masks, The Visuals, The Mystery'
item.description: Ihsahn has no interest in blurring the lines between personal life and stage persona. In his opinion, keeping those worlds apart explains why bands like Ghost, Sleep Token, and Slipknot generate such obsessive fascination.

item.title: DAVE MUSTAINE Recalls METALLICA Audition: 'My Mom Used To Clean Lars' Apartment'
item.description: Dave Mustaine didn’t need to strike a single chord to sense the outcome of his audition for Metallica. After spotting their ad in a magazine, he reached out to Lars Ulrich and arranged to meet up in Newport Beach for a live tryout.

item.title: DUFF MCKAGAN Compares OZZY OSBOURNE to Lemmy, Prince, and Iggy Pop
item.description: Duff McKagan has seen plenty of rock stars come and go, but when it comes to Ozzy Osbourne, he doesn’t mince words. “A constant in rock and roll,” as he puts it.

item.title: DAVE MUSTAINE Says FAITH NO MORE's Mike Patton Is 'An Unprofessional Jerk'
item.description: Dave Mustaine has spent over 40 years running the Megadeth machine as guitarist, vocalist, songwriter, and self-appointed keeper of thrash metal’s purity. In that time, he’s built not only an impressive discography, but a side hustle in speaking his mind with the grace of a sledgehammer.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On Metallica T-Shirts: 'I’m Not Sure I Want Them Wearing That'
item.description: Plenty of metalheads have their rituals. They blast albums, whether on vinyl, cassette, or whatever streaming service rules the moment. They pack venues when the tour bus rolls into town.

item.title: MATT TUCK Says BULLET FOR MY VALENTINE Will Return To Studio: 'We Can't Wait To Drop New Music'
item.description: While stomping around Donington Park for the Download Festival in the UK, Matt Tuck finally offered something resembling an update on Bullet For My Valentine’s elusive eighth studio album.

item.title: DAVID VINCENT Reflects On Fan Expectations: 'Nobody Cares About The New Stuff'
item.description: David Vincent, the former Morbid Angel frontman, isn’t exactly rushing to crank out new material with I Am Morbid. In a recent sit-down with Altars Of Metal, the inevitable question popped up: will I Am Morbid ever release original songs?

item.title: What James Hetfield And Robert Trujillo Would Do If Metallica Never Existed
item.description: Episode 98 of The Metallica Report tossed out a simple question that got James Hetfield and Robert Trujillo thinking about an alternate universe where Metallica never happened. The fan-submitted query from Denmark asked them to picture their lives without the band that has basically defined them.

item.title: David Ellefson: "I Miss Dave" But I’m Done With Megadeth’s Drama
item.description: David Ellefson still feels the absence of Dave Mustaine in his life, even after everything. In a recent chat with The Delz Show, Ellefson reflected: “I miss Dave too.

item.title: Kirk Hammett Rules Out Retirement From Metallica Despite 62 Years of Age
item.description: Kirk Hammett has no interest in slowing down. Speaking to Metal Hammer, he dismissed the idea of retirement entirely. “I don’t believe in retirement. Retirement is something that’s been forced onto people; I don’t believe musicians are allowed to retire,” he said.

item.title: Lzzy Hale Opens Up About New Vocal Mastery After 28 Years Fronting Halestorm
item.description: Long before Lzzy Hale stood under arena lights, she was perched in a dogwood tree somewhere along the Appalachian Trail, testing her voice against the leaves and scaring squirrels.

item.title: James Hetfield Shares The Cost of Fame: ‘They Think They Know Me’
item.description: Metallica’s new documentary, Metallica Saved My Life, made its debut at the Tribeca Festival in New York City on June 11. After the screening, all four band members joined The New Yorker’s Amanda Petrusich for a conversation that pulled back the curtain on both their private lives and the inspiration behind the film.

item.title: David Ellefson Breaks Down Megadeth’s Risk and Its Divisive Legacy
item.description: In 1999, Megadeth rolled the dice with Risk, a record that veered sharply away from the band’s thrash metal identity. For David Ellefson, the album remains, in his own words, “probably the most controversial album in the catalog.

item.title: Vogg Says Decapitated’s New Album is Halfway Done, But When Will It Drop?
item.description: OKAY, SO—Vogg, the guitar wizard of Decapitated, has somehow managed to write 50% of the band’s new album. Fifty. Percent. Not 49%. Not 51%. Exactly half. And he dropped this information like it was no big deal while floating on the 70000 Tons of Metal cruise, which, if you don’t know, is basically a lawless, floating metal festival where dehydration, questionable decisions, and ear-shattering riffs collide on the high seas.

item.title: Dream Theater’s Mike Portnoy on Pain, Perseverance, and Playing Through Injury
item.description: Step into this scene with me… Dream Theater, mid-’90s, prog-metal gods playing Awake on tour—Portnoy’s behind the kit, hair flailing, sticks a blur, sweat dripping like he’s trying to personally refill the Dead Sea.

item.title: Killswitch Engage’s Mike D’Antonio Rejects A.I. Claims: "I Don’t Wanna Be Associated With It"
item.description: Another day, another internet conspiracy theory—this time, aimed at Killswitch Engage bassist and graphic designer Mike D’Antonio, who’s had to crawl out of the art cave he’s been living in for the past eight months just to tell people to shut the hell up about A.

item.title: Clown Admits He Was a “Naysayer” About Revisiting Slipknot’s First Album
item.description: It’s 2025, and somehow Slipknot is still here, still wearing masks, still smashing percussion instruments like cavemen discovering fire, but also—shockingly—getting reflective about their past. Yes, you read that right: Shawn “Clown” Crahan, the band’s resident chaos conductor, actually sat down and got nostalgic.

item.title: Lorraine Lewis on Joining OnlyFans: "It’s Sexy, I’m Owning It, And I’m Having Fun!"
item.description: Lorraine Lewis. 66 years old. Rock icon. Ex-VIXEN. Current FEMME FATALE badass. Also? Now officially on OnlyFans. And not just dipping her toes in—she’s fully in the pool.

item.title: Heidi Shepherd Speaks Out on Vocal Training: “I Was a Singer Before I Was a Screamer”
item.description: Apparently some people still think Heidi Shepherd—frontwoman of BUTCHER BABIES, growler of unholy things, destroyer of vocal cords (except, not hers, more on that later)—can’t sing. And she’s had enough.

item.title: Grammy Interviewer Mistakes Spiritbox’s Courtney LaPlante for Poppy—See the Full Video
item.description: Yeah babe, the Grammys. A night of glitz, glamour, and—if we’re being honest—rock and metal getting shoved to the side like an unwanted side dish at a fancy dinner.

item.title: Max Cavalera on Re-Recording SEPULTURA’s Early Albums: “They Never Sounded Right”
item.description: Oh boy, here we go. Another “let’s redo our old stuff, but this time better” kind of deal. You know, like when you rewrite a high school essay as an adult and suddenly realize, wow, I really didn’t understand metaphors back then.

item.title: Sharon den Adel Confirms Within Temptation’s Next Album Is Taking Shape: “We Have a Clear Vision”
item.description: So Within Temptation has a plan. Well, sort of. Sharon den Adel insists they “really have an idea what we wanna do next,” which sounds promising—until you realize that the band started with the intention of taking their sweet time, only to immediately flip-flop.

item.title: Bush’s Gavin Rossdale on the Music Industry: “I Can’t Work Out How Young Bands Get Paid”
item.description: Gavin Rossdale, frontman of Bush, seems genuinely lost when it comes to figuring out how young bands actually make money these days, and honestly? Same. The guy flat-out said, “I can’t work it out,” and if that isn’t the most relatable statement about the modern music industry, I don’t know what is.

item.title: AVENGED SEVENFOLD's M. Shadows Talks God, Purpose, and Fear
item.description: Deep in conversation on the “Artist Friendly With Joel Madden” podcast, the 43-year-old frontman for AVENGED SEVENFOLD, M. Shadows (real name: Matt Sanders), pulled no punches on religion and spirituality.

item.title: Michael Wilton Talks New Queensrÿche Album and 2025 Goals
item.description: Queensrÿche guitarist Michael Wilton spoke with Robert Cavuoto (for MyGlobalMind). Touched on new record plans? Absolutely. Also reflected on the many twists and turns the band has faced over the decades (and there have been plenty).

item.title: Necrobutcher on Mayhem's Four Decades of Survival
item.description: When the bassist of your band murders the guitarist, you’d think the group might call it quits. Most bands implode over petty squabbles about songwriting credits or tour schedules—not criminal trials.

item.title: L7’s Donita Sparks on the Band’s Unique Place in Rock: ‘We’re an Outlier’
item.description: Donita Sparks from L7—a band often shoved into the ‘90s grunge box but sounding more like MOTÖRHEAD after too much coffee—sat down with Australia’s Heavy. And the question came up: how would she describe their sound?

item.title: John Corabi on Mötley Crüe Exit: "Relieved and Bummed"
item.description: John Corabi (yes, the guy who briefly fronted Mötley Crüe) sat down for an interview and spilled—well, not tea exactly, but maybe lukewarm coffee. His time with the band?

item.title: Ryan McCombs Wishes Social Media Never Existed—But He Still Uses It
item.description: Ryan McCombs—frontman of Drowning Pool and SOIL, master of growls, occasional philosopher—has thoughts about social media. Big ones. Messy ones. The kind that make you nod along until he throws in a time-travel fantasy about stopping Zuckerberg in his tracks (we’ll get there).

item.title: Why Tommy Lee Showers Once a Week, According to His Wife
item.description: Tommy Lee, drummer for Mötley Crüe, bathes sparingly. His wife, Brittany Furlan, says he showers only once a week. The detail emerged on Kaitlyn Bristowe’s Off the Vine podcast, where Furlan spoke about her husband’s habits.

item.title: Linkin Park’s Mike Shinoda: “Our New Lineup Came Together Naturally”
item.description: Linkin Park is back. New album (listen below). New lineup. Same vibe. This one’s called “From Zero”, which feels like a bit of an oversell for a band that’s been rehashing itself since 2017.

item.title: Linkin Park’s Mike Shinoda Talks Brad Delson’s Tour Absence
item.description: Linkin Park’s reunion, complete with a fresh album release last Friday, has been making waves. Yet, the band’s current lineup feels like a revolving door. With Chester Bennington’s tragic loss in 2017 and drummer Rob Bourdon sitting this one out, it’s already a scaled-back return.

item.title: Mike Shinoda on Why Brad Delson Isn’t Touring With Linkin Park
item.description: Brad Delson, the longtime six-string maestro of Linkin Park, is still very much part of the band. In the studio, behind the scenes—he’s there, making things happen. But if you were hoping to see him shred live, prepare for disappointment.

item.title: SKILLET's John Cooper on Political Divides in Rock: "We're Shut Out"
item.description: In a recent chat with the Rebellious Remarks podcast, John Cooper, frontman for SKILLET, took the opportunity to drop some of his usual truth bombs about being a Christian rock musician in today’s ultra-polarized world.

item.title: Ted Nugent Praises Metallica’s "Soulful" Groove While Criticizing Pantera
item.description: In a recent episode of Ted Nugent’s show “Spirit Campfire” on Real America’s Voice, the ever-outspoken Nugent threw a nod to several rockers who are still out there tearing up stages, mentioning Mark Farner, STYX, and Sammy Hagar as some of the enduring performers.

item.title: 'Master Of Puppets' Wins Out for Shavo Odadjian in METALLICA Album Showdown
item.description: When Shavo Odadjian, bassist of SYSTEM OF A DOWN, got hit with the impossible question of whether METALLICA’s “Ride The Lightning” or “Master Of Puppets” was the superior album during an interview with Radioactive MikeZ on 96.

item.title: Phil Labonte: Korn’s Impact on Deathcore Goes Beyond Nu-Metal
item.description: When a band ends up becoming so influential that people start crediting them for launching a whole subgenre, it’s something to take note of. But when a group gets blamed for a genre they don’t even directly belong to?

item.title: Clown on New Slipknot Music: “Delivered in a Way You Can’t Imagine”
item.description: Slipknot has been on a tear lately. Between nostalgia-drenched 25th-anniversary shows and an endless parade of collaborations (because why not?), the band’s summer could be described as anything but boring.

item.title: Metallica's Kirk Hammett Declares Judas Priest the True Founders of Heavy Metal
item.description: Kirk Hammett isn’t here to play revisionist history with metal. When the drummer Carmine Appice tossed out the claim that heavy metal only began with Metallica, some folks had a field day.

item.title: James Hetfield’s Pre-Tour Anxiety: “It’s Just Me and a Rubber Guitar”
item.description: James Hetfield of Metallica has his own brand of anxiety dreams, where his worst-case scenarios aren’t about showing up to class unprepared. No, they involve his bandmates vanishing, his guitar turning into rubber, and feeling like he’s the only one taking things seriously while everyone else is in party mode backstage.

item.title: Jim Root: “Slipknot Is Lucky to Have Eloy Casagrande”
item.description: Slipknot’s Jim Root isn’t holding back his admiration for the band’s newest drumming powerhouse, Eloy Casagrande. If Root’s comments are anything to go by, it seems the band practically stumbled into the perfect fit without breaking a sweat—or even auditioning anyone else.

item.title: Linkin Park Rumored to Return with a Female Lead Singer
item.description: July marks seven years since Chester Bennington’s untimely passing—a moment that shattered not just his family and friends, but the entire world of Linkin Park fans. His death wasn’t just tragic; it was a full stop.

item.title: Korn’s Creative Process: Ray Luzier Breaks Down the Band’s Approach
item.description: Korn’s drummer, Ray Luzier, has been pounding the skins for the band since 2007, and he’s got plenty of stories to tell. In a chat with Modern Drummer, Luzier reflected on some of the band’s most memorable moments, from their biggest hits to their more out-there experiments.

item.title: Amy Lee Reflects on Bring Me to Life's Rap: "Not My Style"
item.description: Amy Lee, the unmistakable voice of Evanescence, hasn’t minced words about her feelings toward the now-iconic rap segment in Bring Me to Life. For two decades, she’s openly expressed her discomfort with the label-driven decision to shoehorn in Paul McCoy’s rap—something neither she nor the band originally envisioned for their breakout hit.
